βουνίτης.definition: dweller on the hills, of Pan

βρυδαλίχα.definition: female mask; also, lewd woman , Id

βιομήχανος.definition: clever at getting a living, Antipho Soph.41; of birds, Arist.HA616b17, al

βελόνη.definition: needle, Batr.130, Eup.259; pipe-fish, Syngnathus, Arist.HA567b23; garfish, Belone acus, ib.506b10, Dorio ap.Ath.7.319d; but prob. f.l. for Archipp.24

βαρβαρόφωνος.definition: speaking a foreign tongue; speaking bad Greek, Str.14.2.28

βαθύκολπος.definition: with dress falling in deep folds; simply, very deep, Nonn.D.12.327; with deep foundations, ib.40.534; set deep, ib.21.94

βαθυκύμων.definition: gen. deep in waves, Musae.189; of Oceanus, Nonn.D.23.320, cf. Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.110

βρίμωσις.definition: indignation, Phld.Ir.p.26 W.: pl., ib.p.52 W

βοηλατέω.definition: drive away oxen, Ar.Fr.758: generally, urge; tend oxen, Lyc.816, Plu.Phil.4

βοήθησις.definition: aid, succour, Hp.Praec.8, dub. in Aen.Tact.16.4; Alex.Aphr.in Sens.98.22

βλάστη.definition: of children, birth from a father, Id.OC972; Id.OT717, cf. Tr.382, Trag.Adesp.373

βοτάνη.definition: herb, Thphr.HP4.4.13, Dsc.1 Praef. 1 , etc; in pl., plants, as material for making clothes, opp. Diog.Oen.10

βοάριος.definition: = Lat. boarius: = forum boarium at Rome, D.H.1.40, cf. D.C.78.25

βούλησις.definition: willing, Arist.de An.433a43; purpose or meaning of a poem, Pl.Prt.344b; signification of a word, Id.Cra.421b

βαθυλήϊος.definition: with deep crop, very fruitful, v.l. for in Il.18.550, cf. A.R.1.830, AP9.110

βορεύς.definition: = in oblique cases Arat.430, 829,882, etc.: nom. pl. Alciphr.1.1

βοώτης.definition: ploughman, Lyc.268, Babr.52.3; the constellation Boötes, Arat.92; but prob. = the star in Od.5.272

βεβαιωτής.definition: one who gives assurance of a thing; legal surety, Plb.2.40.2; Plu.Flam.4; warrantor in sales, SIG2832 , etc

βαθύκληρος.definition: with rich lands, of persons; very rich, of land, Coluth.218, Man.3.239

βρωτήρ.definition: eating, A.Eu.803; Nic.Al.421; . . A.Fr.198: as Subst. in pl., of insects, etc., Orph.L.599; moth, Aq.Is.50.9

βαρύλογος.definition: vented in bitter words, Pi.P.2.55; offensive, of certain Stoic tenets, Phld.Sto.Herc.339.12

βλέννος.definition: slime, Arist.HA591a28; fish allied to Sophr.43, Opp.H.1.109

βλάμμα.definition: = opp. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.71 , Phld.Rh.1.215 S. .; expl. of Gal.18.445

βέλεμνον.definition: poet. for dart, javelin, Il. only in pl., 22.206: later in sg., A.Ag.1496 , cf. 1520, Theoc.11.16; poet., of hail-stones, Orph.L.597

βύσσος.definition: flax, and the linen made from it, Emp.93, Theoc.2.73, etc.; used of perennial flax, Linum angustifolium, grown in Elis, Paus.6.26.6, and of Linum usitatissimum, = Id.5.5.2; also, in later writers, of Indian cotton, Go…

βουβωνίσκος.definition: bandage for the groin, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.55 tit

βομβηδόν.definition: Adv. buzzing, with a hum, A.R.2.133, Luc.Pisc.42

βαλανίτης.definition: acorn-shaped, a; of those who live on acorns, Eust.1859.47

βύθιος.definition: also Gal.2.634:—in the deep; in or of the sea, water animals, AP6.182 ; Poseidon, Luc.Epigr.34; fishery, Opp.H.3.15

βέρεδος.definition: = Lat. veredus, post-horse, Procop.Pers.2.20:—hence Id.Aed.5.3:—also written Secund.Sent.18
